output.subject: We've received your message about your HELOC draw
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for contacting us, and for explaining your situation so clearly. We have received your complaint.

You told us that four days ago you requested a $25,000 draw from your home equity line of credit, which you mentioned was approved last year, so you could pay a deposit to your kitchen contractor. You said the online system still shows the request as "pending review," and you asked why a draw on your own line of credit is being reviewed at all. You also let us know that your contractor is due to start on September 25th and needs his deposit before then, and you asked for the draw to be released.

We understand how stressful it is to wait on funds when a project start date is approaching, and we're sorry for the frustration this has caused.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint, including your question about the review and your request for the funds, and will respond to you within 10 business days.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Time-sensitive: the contractor starts September 25th, which may fall before the 10-business-day response window. Consider whether earlier contact is needed.
Check the current status of the $25,000 draw request and the reason it is pending review.
Decide whether and how to explain the review to the customer. The draft gives no reason and takes no position.
Customer asked for the draw to be released. Decide the outcome before promising anything.
Confirm the line of credit's status and available balance before responding on substance.
